title: Class 6 Science · Ch 2 Worksheet C · Biodiversity & Conservation
instructions: Reflect on biodiversity and how to protect it.

questions.question: Biodiversity refers to
options: the variety of living things in a region
questions.answer: the variety of living things in a region
questions.explanation: Biodiversity = the variety of plants, animals, and microbes in a region.

questions.question: Cutting a forest reduces biodiversity mainly because
options: it removes the homes of many plants and animals
questions.answer: it removes the homes of many plants and animals
questions.explanation: Habitat loss is the main driver of biodiversity loss.

questions.question: Tiny living things visible only through a microscope are called _____.
questions.explanation: Microorganisms include bacteria, amoeba, and yeast.

questions.question: Once a species becomes extinct, we can usually bring it back from another location.
questions.explanation: Extinct means lost forever; recovery is rare and very hard.

questions.question: Why is biodiversity important?
questions.answer: Biodiversity supports food (pollination by bees), medicines, soil fertility, pest control, and balance of nature. Losing it harms human well-being.
questions.explanation: Tests understanding of value of biodiversity.

questions.question: Suggest two simple actions students can take to protect biodiversity in their school surroundings.
questions.answer: Plant native flowering plants to attract local insects and birds; avoid using chemical pesticides; do not litter or pour chemicals into drains; place a bird-bath; respect insects and small animals instead of killing them.

questions.question: Imagine all bees disappear from your area. Describe two effects on plants and one effect on humans.
questions.answer: On plants: many flowering plants would not be pollinated, producing fewer fruits and seeds; some species could decline or vanish. On humans: less food from crops that depend on bee pollination (mango, apple, pumpkin), raising prices and reducing variety in our diet. The example shows how interconnected biodiversity is.
